modules.title: Document Head Setup
modules.learningObjective: Establish base HTML5 boilerplate including character encoding and responsive viewport settings.
modules.lesson: The document head acts as the metadata container for your web page. It does not display content directly to the user but provides essential instructions to the browser, such as character encoding, responsive design scaling, and the page title shown in the browser tab. Setting these up correctly ensures your site renders consistently across different devices and search engines. For example, you can define the language of your content by adding the lang attribute to the html tag: <html lang='en'>.
modules.task:
Your goal is to configure the document head for the Login Greeting Form. Ensure the character set is UTF-8, the viewport is set for mobile responsiveness, and the title is set to 'Login'.

### Requirements
- Set the charset to UTF-8.
- Set the viewport meta tag to width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0.
- Set the document title to 'Login'.

### Example
<meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0'>

### If you're stuck
Check the Hints and References sections for guidance on meta tags.
modules.expectedResult: The browser tab will display the title 'Login', and the page will be correctly configured for responsive scaling on mobile devices.

references.note: Learn about the container for machine-readable information.

modules.title: Body Layout & Heading
modules.learningObjective: Implement structural layout using flex containers to center the content.
modules.lesson:
Flexbox is a powerful layout module that allows you to align items within a container effortlessly. By setting 'display: flex' on a parent element, you can control the distribution of space and the alignment of its children using properties like 'justify-content' and 'align-items'. This is the standard way to center content both horizontally and vertically on a page.

For example, to center a box in the middle of the screen, you apply 'display: flex', 'justify-content: center', and 'align-items: center' to the body element. Remember to set 'min-height: 100vh' so the body takes up the full height of the viewport. A quick snippet: const container = document.querySelector('.box'); container.style.display = 'flex';
modules.task:
### Goal
Implement the base layout for the login page by centering a container on the screen using CSS Flexbox.

### Requirements
- Add a `<style>` block to the `<head>`.
- Apply Flexbox styles to the `body` element to center content.
- Create a `<main>` element with the class `login-card`.
- Add an `<h1>` element with the text 'Welcome' inside the `login-card`.

### Example
```css
.container { display: flex; justify-content: center; }
```

### If you're stuck
Check the Hints and MDN references below for guidance on Flexbox properties.

h1 element exists with text Welcome

modules.lesson:
Forms are the primary way users interact with web applications. By using semantic elements like <label>, <input>, and <button>, you ensure that your interface is accessible and predictable. Labels are particularly important as they provide context for screen readers and improve usability by increasing the clickable area for inputs.

When building forms, always consider the user experience. For example, using the correct input type helps mobile browsers display the appropriate keyboard. A simple snippet for a label and input pair looks like this: <label for='email'>Email</label><input type='email' id='email'>.

modules.title: Inline CSS Styling
modules.learningObjective: Apply dark-themed modern aesthetic styles using CSS properties within the head.
modules.lesson:
CSS allows you to transform plain HTML elements into polished, user-friendly interfaces. By targeting specific tags like inputs and buttons, you can define consistent padding, borders, and color schemes that align with your brand identity. This separation of presentation from structure keeps your code clean and maintainable.

For example, to style a button, you might use: button { background-color: blue; border: none; padding: 10px; }.
modules.task:
Your goal is to enhance the login card by adding specific styles for the input and button elements. 

### Requirements
- Add a CSS rule for the `input` tag with padding, border-radius, border, background, and color.
- Add a CSS rule for the `button` tag with padding, border, border-radius, background, color, font-weight, and cursor.
- Add a CSS rule for the `#greeting` element to ensure it has a minimum height and no margin.

### Example
```css
input { padding: 0.5rem; border: 1px solid #ccc; }
```

If you're stuck, check the hints and MDN references provided below.

modules.title: Inline JavaScript Behavior
modules.learningObjective: Script the logic to capture input value and conditionally update the DOM greeting output.
modules.lesson:
JavaScript allows you to make your web pages interactive by responding to user actions. By selecting DOM elements and attaching event listeners, you can capture input data and dynamically update the content of your page without needing to refresh the browser. This creates a seamless experience where the interface reacts to the user in real-time.

For example, you can change the color of a button when it is clicked: `button.addEventListener('click', () => { button.style.backgroundColor = 'red'; });`.
modules.task:
### Goal
Implement the logic to capture the username from the input field and display a personalized greeting when the 'Log in' button is clicked.

### Requirements
- Use `document.getElementById` to reference the input, button, and greeting elements.
- Add a 'click' event listener to the button.
- Use `input.value.trim()` to get the user's name.
- Update `greeting.textContent` to 'Hello, <name>!' if a name is provided, or 'Please enter your username.' if the input is empty.

### Example
```javascript
const btn = document.querySelector('#my-btn');
btn.addEventListener('click', () => console.log('Clicked!'));
```

If you're stuck, check the hints and MDN references provided below.
modules.expectedResult: The application will display 'Hello, [Name]!' when a user enters a name and clicks 'Log in', or 'Please enter your username.' if the field is left blank.
